title: Build a press kit page with logos, screenshots, boilerplate and a fact sheet, by Fri 20 Nov
description: Journalists, podcast hosts and partners need one place to grab accurate facts about Zedu without emailing the team. A person supplies the final logo files and screenshots, and confirms every number. Nothing is invented. Done when the page copy, fact sheet and asset list are approved and a person has published the page.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build the press kit from a fact register with named team checks
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Make one checklist of every press-kit item and track its source, owner and status: draft, awaiting confirmation, or approved. Draft the short and long company descriptions from public, verified Zedu information; leave numbers, names, contact details and claims out until the team confirms them. Pair each approved text item with the logo or screenshot needed, note the exact asset format and owner, and list gaps for the team to supply. This gives journalists one consistent, accurate kit and prevents unverified facts from reaching the published page.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Comprehensive Media Kit with Downloadable Brand Assets and Verified Story Angles
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Assemble an online press kit containing vector SVG logos, executive bios, high-res UI mockups, and a 1-page fact sheet. Package with 3 timely story angles on the future of low-bandwidth cohort education in Africa.

upvotes.reason: Specific deliverable with clear scope and measurable outcome.

zedu.chat has no press page today: /press and /media both return 200 with the generic app-shell title 'Zedu - Seamless Video Meetings & Learning Communities' (22 Oct 2026), and the live site shows no address, phone or press email. A media kit with downloadable assets and checked story angles fills that gap, as long as every story angle is sourced.
Media kit with verified story angles and downloadable assets

downvotes.reason: The accepted press-kit approach cmvjdemm3033h122moo507dqd already covers approved descriptions, fact sheet, named confirmations and logo/screenshot assets. A second online media kit repeats that deliverable; story angles can be added to the existing kit or pitching work. The goal specifically needs six real product screenshots, so mockups should not replace the required live captures.
It promises 'high-res UI mockups' and executive bios, but the goal requires real product screenshots and only team-approved names and numbers.

A press kit built on high-res UI mockups puts invented screens next to a fact sheet about the real product, and press will treat the two as the same thing. It should carry real screenshots, and the low-bandwidth story needs the measured byte budget behind it.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Give journalists a 'what we can't confirm yet' box beside the fact sheet
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Early-stage stories breed questions; answering 'not yet' in writing keeps press moving without inventing. Approach: alongside the accepted fact register, add a fixed box to the press kit: the questions journalists usually ask first (funding, users, revenue, app details, public roadmap) marked clearly as not public, each with what we can say instead. No estimates, nothing beyond the register. Tasks: the 'not yet public' box (content), register alignment (research).
